# CORE-SEC-04

**Does a threat model exist for this version of the design, and has the cybersecurity assessment been handed over?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [Core architecture lens](core.md) 0.6.0 |
| Area | SEC: Security architecture |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A tool, by its rule |
| Reads | `evidence.type` |

## Why it matters

Threat modelling analyses the same representation an architecture assessment reads; it belongs with the design. Whether controls are implemented and effective does not, and is handed over.

## Rule

evidence has an entry of type threat-model; a design with status accepted or active also has security-assessment, or the assessment records a hand-over to cybersecurity.

## Sources

- Threat Modeling Manifesto (`tmm`)
- NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments (`nist-800-30`)
- The Open Group, G152, Integrating Risk and Security within a TOGAF Enterprise Architecture (`togaf-g152`)
